decisions.reason: As a new safety shoe line in the firm's core business, Product A fits the publicly stated innovation path and, with launch investment already made and no clear failure evidence yet, management would be inclined to continue it.

Product B extends the core footwear offer with a complementary comfort insole, so sunk development and commercialization effort plus its strategic fit with tailored solutions make continued support more likely than an early withdrawal.

Because Product C is a close adjacence to the firm's protective-footwear business and no decisive negative market signal is reported, management would likely justify staying the course and treat any weak uptake as temporary.

Product D received a dedicated page of its own, indicating a visible public commitment, and its ergonomic positioning aligns closely with the firm's innovation narrative, which strongly favors persistence.

Product E broadens the firm's protective-footwear expertise into a demanding professional segment, and a large established German manufacturer would likely maintain it at least longer to recoup investment and validate the launch.
Product F was shown on the home page, signaling especially visible commitment, so under escalation of commitment management would be reluctant to retreat quickly and would continue backing it.
